mechanism: Scopolamine's anticholinergic effects can reduce gastrointestinal motility and fluid secretion, potentially impairing torsemide absorption and enhancing volume depletion effects when combined with loop diuretic-induced electrolyte losses.
action: Monitor fluid and electrolyte status closely; ensure adequate hydration and consider electrolyte supplementation; assess for anticholinergic adverse effects that may be potentiated by diuretic-induced dehydration.
